authorization: Owner requested selective integration and a contextual optional reference on 2026-09-07. This authorizes candidate development, not installation or release.
strategy: COMPOSE / ADAPT existing source, graph planner, turn-task and forthcoming path/readiness contracts; no new clinical scoring system

rules.title: Readiness is present adult capacity, not perfect healing
rules.guidance: Before encouraging romantic escalation, distinguish loneliness and longing from demonstrated ability to handle intimacy responsibly. When substantial current foreseeable harm remains, recommend pausing active romance-seeking and building structured non-romantic support. Do not offer romance as the treatment for instability.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Owner-requested safety application, not a validated clinical score or authority to forbid an adult. Assess current function, risks, supports and trajectory rather than a diagnosis or hospitalization history alone. Reassess a pause as capacity changes. Actual-child responsibilities apply where children exist or the contemplated activity could create them; do not assume everybody wants children. Natural adult capacities count without requiring a parts vocabulary or prescribed technique.
rules.progressCheck: Look for demonstrated self-care, respect for refusal, accountability and support not contingent on obtaining a partner. Affirmations, insight, feeling loved or agreement with the helper do not by themselves establish readiness.

rules.title: Wanting, loving and suitability are distinct
rules.guidance: Preserve the guide’s distinction between eros (wanting) and agape/metta (care for the other person’s wellbeing). Desire need not be shamed, but being wanted, intense closeness and suitability for a relationship are not interchangeable evidence.
rules.scopeAdaptation: The requirement for both forms of love is the owner’s relationship philosophy, not a diagnostic test. Ask about the person’s actual experience and goals rather than imposing a label.
rules.progressCheck: Test whether care includes the other person’s boundaries and welfare when these conflict with obtaining reassurance or closeness.

rules.title: Demonstrated capacity outranks an impressive healing story
rules.guidance: Use recent ordinary interactions and conflicts to understand current capacity: what happened, what each person did, how repair occurred and what changed afterward. Large progress from a difficult starting point can coexist with serious remaining limitations. A deep conversation is different evidence from functioning together.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Distinguish testimony, direct observation, interpretation and unknowns. Do not automatically contact partners, exes or friends, adjudicate an absent person, or treat a polished answer as proof.
rules.progressCheck: A new interpretation, mutual disclosure, or model praise is not a substitute for changed conduct in a comparable real situation.

rules.title: Avoid stacking entanglements before evidence catches up
rules.guidance: Separate wanting someone from choosing sex, cohabitation, shared finances or parenthood. Where pacing is relevant, discuss practical boundaries before high-pressure situations. One rapid step does not justify accelerating every subsequent step.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Adapt to the actual relationship stage; do not invent fixed waiting periods, demand perfect certainty, or prescribe provoking a conflict to test a partner. An imagination exercise generates questions, not predictions.
rules.progressCheck: Check whether the agreed boundary survives attraction and whether new evidence, rather than sunk costs or attachment alone, supports the next commitment.

rules.title: Reciprocal care is not permanent therapist-parent outsourcing
rules.guidance: Welcome mutual support and complementary strengths while noticing when one partner becomes the default parent, therapist or sole support system. Bring in other support and reconsider the arrangement rather than merely asking the overloaded partner to soothe better.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Needing help or receiving care does not itself prove dependency. Distinguish temporary or accommodated support from loss of agency, entitlement and responsibilities that one person cannot sustainably carry.
rules.progressCheck: Observe actual burden, agency, boundaries and whether roles can vary. Calmer feelings alongside rising dependency are not an uncomplicated success.

rules.title: Community needs its own purpose and privacy boundaries
rules.guidance: Build support beyond the couple: friendship, meaningful activity, mentoring and appropriate outside help. Examine whether support-building is being replaced by partner-seeking. Maintain enough outside perspective to notice patterns the relationship obscures.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Do not infer hidden romantic motives from wanting a partner alone. Use evidence of goal substitution. Shared community is an option, not a guarantee of safety; private/confidential support may be essential, especially with coercion. No forced disclosure or social isolation.
rules.progressCheck: Ask whether the support remains useful when no romantic opportunity results, and whether practical stability and agency improve rather than attention simply moving to one prospective rescuer.

rules.title: Make agreements concrete without pretending to control feelings
rules.guidance: Clarify what the relationship and its commitments mean to each person: chosen actions, boundaries, caregiving and responsibilities if circumstances change. Consent and privacy remain live. No one owes disclosure or enactment of a fantasy.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Treat the guide’s position on promises of feelings as the owner’s philosophy. Do not mandate monogamy, non-monogamy, radical disclosure or a particular meaning of marriage. A request for connection is not consent to sexual or spiritual discussion.
rules.progressCheck: Look for mutually understood, freely chosen agreements and observed follow-through, not agreement labels alone.

rules.title: Coercion is not a mutual growth exercise
rules.guidance: When someone fears refusal, truth-telling or leaving, prioritize practical safety and suitable outside support. Do not frame terrorizing or controlling conduct as two equally responsible inner children, a communication drill, or a spiritual crucible they must endure.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Safety support does not require proving a diagnosis or an absent person’s motive. Do not require joint confrontation, mediation or disclosure to an unsafe partner. The ordinary safety route outranks romance exploration and external reading.
rules.progressCheck: Judge change by safer choices and access to support, not compliance, a temporary calm, forgiveness or preserving the relationship.

rules.title: Check present relational reality before explaining jealousy inwardly
rules.guidance: Distinguish observable conduct and actual agreements from interpretations. Jealousy can accompany a real relational problem or an inflated threat; do not assume either. Address concrete external problems before reflexively searching childhood for the explanation.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Do not certify mind-reading, recovered history, infidelity or pathology from a one-sided account. One person’s feeling can be valid while its explanation remains uncertain.
rules.progressCheck: The useful next inquiry should discriminate present evidence from an old expectation, rather than provide repeated reassurance or accumulate more theory.

rules.title: Children’s care is distinct from the fate of romance
rules.guidance: Include responsibilities to existing or possible children when relevant. Consider whether care and safe cooperation could survive relationship change; do not recruit children into adult conflict. Whether romance continues is not the only outcome that matters.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Planning is not proof of future parenting capacity. Do not invent children, predict inevitable custody loss, give jurisdiction-specific legal advice from an essay, or require unsafe contact in the name of co-parenting.
rules.progressCheck: Track concrete care arrangements and reduced exposure to adult conflict separately from whether the adults reconcile.

rules.title: Benefit requires transfer, not just a powerful state
rules.guidance: A profound exercise, felt bond or moment of relief may be real without demonstrating everyday compatibility or durable change. Revisit what changed in ordinary life: clearer needs, less combative communication, respected boundaries, workable action or more agency.
rules.scopeAdaptation: The guide gives a one-to-two-week communication example in its Measuring the benefits section. This is an example, not a universal clinical threshold. Carry the transfer criterion into the path controller without importing the surrounding drug recommendations or promoting intense states.
rules.progressCheck: Compare the path’s prediction with actual follow-through. Relief plus worsening dependency, repeated unchanged conflict, destabilization or no new useful information warrants review or a different route, not a more elaborate repetition.

rules.title: Repair, restructure and end are genuinely different paths
rules.guidance: Distinguish whether to continue a relationship from how to leave responsibly. Repair, less intensity, friendship, separation and ending can be different honest outcomes. Outside help may change a stuck conversation; one person cannot supply the other’s participation.
rules.scopeAdaptation: Do not automatically tell an existing couple to separate because new dating would currently be unwise. Do not demand endless counseling, self-work, disclosure or unsafe contact; practical safety, children and other responsibilities constrain the next action.
rules.progressCheck: If the same repair effort repeatedly yields no change, reconsider the aim and level of support, rather than treating preserving romance as the fixed success criterion.

polarity.boundary: Discuss meaning, chosen roles and equal dignity only when the adult raises it. Do not install gender generalizations as facts or performance demands.

spiritual-romance.boundary: Preserve spiritual significance without certifying destiny, unique soul identity, reciprocity or permission to ignore refusal and harm. The guide itself de-ontologizes twin flames.

relationship-forms.boundary: Contextual values discussion, not compulsory monogamy, polyamory, marriage, celibacy or casual sex.

sexual-communication.boundary: Non-graphic consent, compatibility, privacy and communication are within the bounded support lens. The full adult guide is optional, not sexual technique instruction.

notImported.category: Medical, contraceptive, anatomical and drug-treatment claims or instructions
notImported.disposition: Do not install as clinical guidance. Separate evidence and safety review would be required; a link is not a substitute for that review.

notImported.category: Autobiographical allegations, diagnostic interpretations and population-level biological or historical generalizations
notImported.disposition: Retain as source context, not public client examples, diagnostic rules, or independently established facts.

notImported.category: Explicit techniques and optional spiritual/archetypal material
notImported.disposition: Do not load wholesale into therapy turns or expose the full guide to a minor or unknown-age audience. No link to facilitate coercive, unsafe or medical practice.

limits: Policy data and deterministic scope tests are not clinical validation or live model fidelity evidence.
No client memory, persistence, provider calls, graph mutation, installed-guide change or release is implemented by this supplement.
A date-ready certification, a fixed recovery duration, a percentage healed and a diagnosis-based permanent dating ban are deliberately absent.
